set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which laboratory abnormalities are common in erysipelas, and what do they contribute?
opts: Leukocytosis with raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein — common but not diagnostic
Correct. The diagnosis remains clinical in a classic presentation.
Thrombocytopenia with mild hyponatraemia and transaminitis — and diagnostic in almost every case
That is the Rocky Mountain spotted fever pattern.
Eosinophilia with a raised immunoglobulin E — diagnostic when combined with the rash
That pattern is not described for erysipelas.
Entirely normal inflammatory markers — which is what confirms the diagnosis
Inflammatory markers are commonly raised.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is recurrent folliculitis in a Staphylococcus aureus carrier treated?
opts: Topical clindamycin applied twice daily to the affected follicles for a month
Topical antibiotic creams treat mild infection rather than carriage.
Mupirocin ointment applied in the nasal vestibule twice daily for five days
Correct. Carriage of the organism in the nose sustains recurrence.
Oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole taken twice daily for a ten-day course
Oral therapy is used for extensive infection or resistant organisms.
Chlorhexidine washes to the affected areas daily for a two-week period
Antibacterial soaps are advised but nasal decolonisation is the specific measure.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What are the mandatory safety requirements for oral isotretinoin?
opts: Weekly complete blood counts throughout the course, with pregnancy testing left to clinical judgement
Pregnancy testing is mandatory rather than discretionary.
Baseline electrocardiogram and monthly potassium levels, with contraception advised but not required
Two effective forms of contraception are preferred, one a barrier method.
Negative pregnancy tests before, monthly during and five weeks after treatment, with iPledge enrolment
Correct. Only one month is dispensed at a time and blood donation is prohibited.
Negative pregnancy tests before treatment only, with liver function checked at the end of the course
Testing continues monthly and for five weeks afterwards.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is chronic paronychia treated?
opts: Topical mupirocin applied to the nail fold three times daily until the swelling settles
Mupirocin is an antibacterial used for impetigo and staphylococcal carriage.
Keep the hands dry and use a broad-spectrum topical antifungal, with oral fluconazole in severe cases
Correct — treat the underlying inflammation and infection together.
Warm soaks three times daily with incision and drainage if purulent material has collected
That is the treatment of acute paronychia.
Oral cephalexin for ten days with removal of the nail plate if there is no early response
Antibacterial therapy does not address the usual candidal cause.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which statement about preventing hot tub folliculitis is correct?
opts: Raising the water temperature above forty degrees kills the organism responsible
Temperature is not the control measure described.
Wearing a rash guard in the water prevents the organism reaching the follicles
Barrier clothing is not among the preventive measures given.
Showering after contact does not prevent it; continuous filtration and disinfectant monitoring do
Correct, along with frequent changing of the water.
Showering immediately after contact reliably prevents it if done within thirty minutes
Showering afterwards is specifically stated not to prevent infection.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which acne lesions are classed as non-inflammatory?
opts: Open comedones (blackheads) and closed comedones (whiteheads)
Correct. Papules, pustules and nodules make up the inflammatory group.
Papules and pustules arising on a background of facial erythema
Both of those are classed as inflammatory lesions.
Nodules and cysts that heal with atrophic or hypertrophic scars
Nodules are inflammatory lesions.
Telangiectasias and persistent flushing of the central cheeks
Those are features of rosacea, not acne.

set1.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: When should cultures be obtained in impetigo?
opts: In every case at first presentation, since staphylococcal and streptococcal disease are treated differently from one another
Impetigo is most often diagnosed by clinical appearance alone.
Only when the lesions have failed to respond after a full two-week course of topical mupirocin
Culture is directed by resistance risk and complications, not treatment duration.
Only in children under three years of age, since they are the group at highest risk of complications
Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis particularly affects three to seven year olds.
When the patient is at high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, or when post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis is present
Correct — a health-care worker or teacher is the example given of high risk.

set1.io: Objective d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: How does the sex distribution of acne differ between adolescence and adulthood?
opts: Adolescent acne is more common and severe in females; post-adolescent acne is more common in men
That reverses both halves of the stated pattern.
Adolescent acne affects both sexes equally; post-adolescent acne is far more common in men
Adolescent disease is specifically described as more common and severe in males.
Adolescent acne is more common in males; post-adolescent acne affects both sexes about equally
Post-adolescent acne is specifically more common in women than men.
Adolescent acne is more common and severe in males; post-adolescent acne is more common in women
Correct. Post-adolescent acne is defined here as acne over 25 years of age.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which shaving advice is given for pseudofolliculitis barbae?
opts: Shave daily against the grain with a multi-blade razor to cut hairs below the surface
Cutting hair below the surface is what allows it to re-enter the skin.
Shave weekly with an electric razor set to the closest possible cutting length
The closest cut is the problem rather than the solution.
Continue the current routine and treat each papule with a topical antibiotic
The shaving technique itself has to change.
Stop shaving if possible, use clean razors, and avoid lift-and-cut razor systems
Correct — mild razor angles and single or at most double blades are preferred.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which lesion type is characteristic of hidradenitis suppurativa on examination?
opts: The double comedone — a blackhead with two or more openings
Correct, alongside nodules, sinus tracts, abscesses and meshlike scarring.
The honey-coloured adherent crust overlying a superficial erosion
That is non-bullous impetigo.
The follicular pustule pierced by a single central hair shaft
That is folliculitis.
The tense clear bulla that leaves a collarette after rupture
That is bullous impetigo.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What distinguishes ecthyma from ordinary impetigo?
opts: It deepens into a dermal ulceration with a thicker grey-yellow crust, heals slowly and scars
Correct, usually on the lower extremities, with regional lymphadenopathy common.
It remains confined to the epidermis, resolves within a week and never leaves a scar behind
That describes ordinary impetigo rather than ecthyma.
It produces tense bullae on intact skin that rupture to leave shallow moist erosions
That describes bullous impetigo.
It spreads rapidly along superficial lymphatics with a sharply demarcated raised edge
That describes erysipelas.

set1.io: Objective d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set1.q: Which oral antibiotic is described as the drug of choice for impetigo in children?
opts: Dicloxacillin
It is listed as an option but not the paediatric drug of choice.
Erythromycin
It is not the agent named for children here.
Cephalexin
Correct. Clindamycin is used where there is penicillin allergy.
Doxycycline
Doxycycline is limited to children over eight years old.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the defining physical finding of erysipelas?
opts: A honey-coloured crust firmly adherent over a superficial epidermal erosion
That is non-bullous impetigo.
A plaque raised above the level of surrounding skin with a clear line of demarcation
Correct. Lower extremities are involved in 80% of patients, with red streaks toward lymph nodes.
An area of erythema whose borders are neither elevated nor sharply demarcated
That is the finding that rules erysipelas out and points to cellulitis.
A firm tender nodule with a single central opening and surrounding erythema
That is a furuncle.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is a carbuncle?
opts: A single furuncle larger than five millimetres across
Size alone does not make a furuncle a carbuncle.
A furuncle that has become secondarily infected with yeast
Secondary yeast infection is not what defines it.
A furuncle that has failed to respond to oral antibiotics
Treatment response is not part of the definition.
Two or more confluent furuncles with separate heads
Correct — interconnecting furuncles arising in several hair follicles.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the pharmacologic treatment of erysipelas?
opts: Mupirocin ointment, with oral dicloxacillin if lesions are widespread
That regimen belongs to impetigo.
Doxycycline, with benzoyl peroxide added to reduce bacterial resistance
That combination belongs to acne vulgaris.
Penicillin V, with clindamycin if the patient is penicillin allergic
Correct. Prompt treatment matters because progression can be rapid.
Cephalexin, with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole if purulence is present
That regimen belongs to cellulitis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which complication may follow impetigo, and can antibiotics prevent it?
opts: Toxic shock syndrome, which topical mupirocin has been shown to prevent
That is not the complication described.
Acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, which antibiotics do not prevent
Correct — the immune activation usually precedes antibiotic treatment.
Acute rheumatic fever, which prompt antibiotic treatment reliably prevents
Rheumatic fever is not the complication named for impetigo here.
Necrotizing fasciitis, which early oral antibiotics prevent in most cases
That is a separate condition requiring surgical debridement.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which four factors underlie acne vulgaris?
opts: Androgen deficiency, keratin thinning, fungal overgrowth and vascular ectasia
None of these appears among the four factors for acne.
Follicular hyperkeratinisation, increased sebum, Cutibacterium acnes and inflammation
Correct. The temporal sequence between the four is not fully understood.
Follicular atrophy, reduced sebum, Staphylococcus aureus and lymphatic obstruction
Each element is the opposite of, or unrelated to, what the lecture names.
Apocrine duct occlusion, friction, secondary infection and follicular scarring
Those are the predisposing factors listed for hidradenitis suppurativa.

set1.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: Why will antibiotics not work on the devitalised area in a cellulitic limb?
opts: The organism in devitalised tissue is always methicillin resistant
The problem is delivery rather than resistance.
Devitalised tissue destroys antibiotic molecules on contact
That is not the described mechanism.
Oral antibiotics never reach the subcutaneous tissue at all
They do, where the tissue is perfused.
It is not perfused, so the drug never reaches the site
Correct — tense, cyanotic, necrotic, bronzed or blanched tissue needs debridement.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which risk factors are named for erysipelas?
opts: Puberty, androgen excess, a first-degree family history, lithium and systemic corticosteroids
Those are predisposing factors for acne vulgaris.
Impaired lymphatic drainage, immunocompromise, tinea pedis, obesity, trauma and pre-existing impetigo
Correct. Mastectomy is the example given of impaired lymphatic drainage.
Repeated hand immersion in water, occupational chemical contact, diabetes and nail biting
Those are predisposing factors for paronychia.
Hot weather, excessive perspiration, apocrine duct obstruction, obesity and cigarette smoking
Those are predisposing factors for hidradenitis suppurativa.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which risk factors are named for necrotizing fasciitis?
opts: Mastectomy, tinea pedis, obesity and any pre-existing superficial skin infection
Those are the risk factors for erysipelas.
Manicure, hangnail, ingrown nail and the habit of biting or picking at the nails
Those are predisposing factors for acute paronychia.
Trauma, burns, surgery, immunosuppression, renal failure, alcoholism, dental infection and injection drug use
Correct, and it occurs more often in males than females.
Obesity, poor hygiene, occlusive clothing, hot humid weather and nasal staphylococcal carriage
Those are the risk factors for folliculitis.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the expected course of cellulitis on antibiotic therapy?
opts: It may look worse on day one, fever usually resolves within twenty-four hours, inflammation over one to two weeks
Correct. Fever beyond forty-eight hours prompts a change guided by culture.
It improves visibly within hours, fever resolves within six hours, and erythema clears within three days
That is faster than the described course.
It worsens for the first week before any improvement, with fever expected to persist throughout
Fever persisting beyond forty-eight hours is a reason to change therapy.
It resolves without any change in appearance, since the erythema is not caused by the infection
The erythema is part of the infection.

set1.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set1.q: Which patients are given as examples of high risk for methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in the impetigo section?
opts: A health-care worker or a teacher
Correct. Culture is obtained in those patients rather than in every case.
A child under three or an infant
Age alone is not the example given for resistance risk.
A swimmer or a laundry worker
Those occupations predispose to chronic paronychia.
A bartender or a professional cook
Those occupations also predispose to chronic paronychia.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: By what mechanisms do oral contraceptive pills improve acne?
opts: Estrogen suppresses Cutibacterium acnes directly and reduces follicular hyperkeratinisation
Those are the actions of antimicrobials and retinoids respectively.
Estrogen decreases sebum, suppresses ovarian androgens and raises sex hormone binding globulin
Correct. Raising that globulin lowers circulating free testosterone.
Estrogen increases sebum, stimulates ovarian androgens and lowers sex hormone binding globulin
Every clause reverses the actual effect.
Progestin blocks the androgen receptor within the sebaceous gland and reduces keratinisation
That is not the mechanism the lecture describes.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: What is the mainstay of treatment for a carbuncle?
opts: Incision and drainage, with endocarditis prophylaxis for at-risk patients
Correct, alongside oral antibiotics chosen for the likely organism.
Warm compresses alone, since most carbuncles drain without intervention
Warm compresses are usually sufficient only for small furuncles.
Oral antibiotics alone, since drainage risks seeding the bloodstream
Drainage is the mainstay rather than a hazard to avoid.
Wide surgical excision of the affected area under general anaesthesia
Wide excision is the curative option in hidradenitis suppurativa.

set1.io: Objective c — Differentiate primary from secondary bacterial infection of the skin
set1.q: What is the primary portal of entry for impetigo?
opts: Minor superficial breaks in the skin such as cuts and bug bites
Correct. No predisposing lesion is identified in most patients.
An occluded apocrine duct that ruptures into the surrounding dermis
That mechanism belongs to hidradenitis suppurativa.
A hair follicle already inflamed by shaving or occlusive clothing
That mechanism belongs to folliculitis and furuncles.
Traumatic inoculation of bacteria deep into the dermal tissues
That mechanism describes abscess formation.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which oral antibiotic is specifically suggested for paronychia after nail biting?
opts: Doxycycline, because of exposure to oral flora
Doxycycline is not the agent named for this exposure.
Ciprofloxacin, because of exposure to oral flora
Ciprofloxacin is named for resistant Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Penicillin V, because of exposure to oral flora
Penicillin V is the erysipelas treatment.
Clindamycin, because of exposure to oral flora
Correct. Amoxicillin-clavulanate and cephalexin are the other named options.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is acute paronychia treated?
opts: Oral antibiotics alone in all cases, since incision of the nail fold risks permanent deformity
Incision and drainage is used in severe cases.
Warm soaks for twenty minutes three times daily in mild cases; incision and drainage in severe cases
Correct, with oral antibiotics and cultures to rule out resistant organisms where appropriate.
A broad-spectrum topical antifungal in all cases, with oral fluconazole if the disease is severe
That is the treatment of chronic paronychia.
Immediate nail plate removal in all cases, since the nail harbours the responsible organism
Nail removal is not the described treatment.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: How is a cutaneous abscess treated?
opts: Oral antibiotics alone in every case, since incision risks spreading the infection into the blood
Incision and drainage is the treatment when it does not drain on its own.
Warm compresses alone in every case, since abscesses reliably resolve without any intervention
That approach suits small furuncles rather than abscesses.
Wide surgical excision of the affected area, since recurrence is otherwise close to universal
Wide excision belongs to hidradenitis suppurativa.
Surgical incision and drainage if it does not drain spontaneously; warm soaks and antibiotics if it does
Correct. Broad-spectrum cover considers methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, then narrows to culture.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which organism most commonly causes bacterial folliculitis?
opts: Corynebacterium minutissimum, with Candida albicans occasionally present
That organism causes erythrasma.
Cutibacterium acnes, with Staphylococcus epidermidis occasionally involved
Cutibacterium acnes is the organism of acne vulgaris.
Staphylococcus aureus, with Pseudomonas aeruginosa occasionally responsible
Correct. Folliculitis can also be fungal, viral, physical or chemical in origin.
Streptococcus pyogenes, with Staphylococcus aureus occasionally responsible
Group A streptococcus is the leading organism in erysipelas.

set1.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set1.q: Which organism causes erythrasma and where does it live?
opts: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, entering the follicle from inadequately chlorinated water
That organism causes hot tub folliculitis.
Staphylococcus aureus, releasing epidermolytic toxins that split the epidermis
That mechanism produces bullous impetigo.
Corynebacterium minutissimum, invading the upper third of the stratum corneum
Correct. Heat and humidity are the favourable conditions; diabetics are high risk.
Candida albicans, colonising the space beneath a separated proximal nail fold
That is the organism of chronic paronychia.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Why is benzoyl peroxide added when a topical or oral antibiotic is used for acne?
opts: It prevents the photosensitivity that tetracyclines can cause
Sun protection is advised separately and is not achieved this way.
It shortens the course of oral antibiotic therapy to two weeks
Oral courses are kept to three to four months for resistance.
It decreases the development of antibiotic resistance
Correct, and it is also keratolytic and anti-inflammatory in its own right.
It increases the absorption of the antibiotic into the follicle
That is not the stated reason for combining them.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How does a carbuncle differ from a furuncle at presentation?
opts: It presents as a single opening with a surrounding zone of erythema
That is the furuncle. Carbuncles have sieve-like multiple openings.
It presents as a plaque raised above the skin with a demarcated edge
That describes erysipelas.
It is extremely painful and more often produces malaise, chills and fever
Correct. Systemic symptoms are more common with a carbuncle.
It is painless and produces no systemic symptoms of any kind at all
Carbuncles are described as extremely painful.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Why should topical tretinoin and benzoyl peroxide not be applied at the same time?
opts: Because tretinoin blocks the antimicrobial effect that benzoyl peroxide has
No such interaction is described.
Because of the risk of skin irritation, so at least three hours should separate them
Correct. That interval is specified in the patient education.
Because benzoyl peroxide inactivates tretinoin, so alternate days are recommended
Irritation, not inactivation, is the stated reason.
Because the combination raises the risk of photosensitivity in treated areas
Sun sensitivity is a separate caution about acne treatments generally.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What does the 2016 American Academy of Dermatology guideline recommend for comedonal acne?
opts: A topical antimicrobial with a topical retinoid, or benzoyl peroxide with an antibiotic
That is the recommendation for mild papulopustular and mixed acne.
A topical retinoid with an oral antibiotic and topical benzoyl peroxide together
That is the recommendation for moderate papulopustular and mixed acne.
Oral isotretinoin as monotherapy over a sixteen to twenty week treatment course
That is an option for severe nodular acne.
A topical retinoid, switching to azelaic or salicylic acid if it is not tolerated
Correct. That is the entry point of the treatment ladder.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: A child with impetigo has lesions too numerous and widespread for topical mupirocin. Which oral options apply?
opts: Doxycycline, minocycline or sarecycline for a three-month course
Those are the oral tetracyclines used in acne.
Dicloxacillin, amoxicillin-clavulanate, cephalexin, or clindamycin if penicillin allergic
Correct — cephalexin is the drug of choice in children.
Penicillin V, or else clindamycin if the patient reports a penicillin allergy
That regimen belongs to erysipelas.
Ciprofloxacin, linezolid, or trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole
Those cover resistant organisms rather than being first-line here.

set2.io: Objective d — Medical care strategies across infant, adolescent, adult and elderly populations
set2.q: What isolation advice is given for a child with impetigo?
opts: No isolation is needed at any point, since impetigo does not spread person to person
Impetigo is described as very contagious and autoinoculable.
Isolate for a full ten days from the appearance of the very first crusted lesion
That is longer than the interval given.
Isolate until treatment has been underway for twenty-four to forty-eight hours
Correct, and do not share towels, clothing, bath water, washcloths or razors.
Isolate until every crusted lesion has completely healed and the skin is clear
The stated interval is tied to starting treatment, not to healing.

set2.io: Objective c — Differentiate primary from secondary bacterial infection of the skin
set2.q: How does a cutaneous abscess differ in origin from a furuncle?
opts: An abscess arises from an infected hair follicle, whereas a furuncle follows traumatic inoculation of bacteria
That reverses the two mechanisms.
An abscess arises from an obstructed apocrine gland, whereas a furuncle follows a break in the epidermis
Apocrine obstruction is the mechanism of hidradenitis suppurativa.
An abscess arises from lymphatic spread of streptococci, whereas a furuncle spreads along the dermis
Neither mechanism is described that way.
An abscess usually follows traumatic inoculation of bacteria, whereas a furuncle arises from an infected follicle
Correct. Abscesses are often polymicrobial, with Staphylococcus aureus the commonest organism.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What must not be allowed to happen in suspected necrotizing fasciitis?
opts: Laboratory tests and imaging must not delay surgical intervention
Correct — it is a surgical emergency with high mortality.
Broad-spectrum antibiotics must not be started before cultures return
Antibiotics are given broadly and early.
The patient must not be admitted to a burn or trauma centre
That is exactly where they should be admitted.
A team approach must not delay the primary surgeon's decision
Consultations are described as needed rather than as a delay.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the natural course of hot tub folliculitis?
opts: Progressive without oral ciprofloxacin in every patient
Most cases resolve without specific treatment.
Chronic and relapsing for months after a single exposure
The condition clears within days.
Resolving only after the affected follicles are drained
Drainage is not part of the management.
Usually self-limiting, clearing in two to ten days
Correct — ciprofloxacin is reserved for widespread or resistant cases.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How does acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis present after impetigo?
opts: Painless jaundice with pale stools and progressive weight loss
That picture is unrelated to this complication.
Sudden oedema, haematuria with smoky or tea-coloured urine, proteinuria and hypertension
Correct — especially in three to seven year olds.
Migratory arthritis, a new heart murmur and subcutaneous nodules over the elbows
That describes acute rheumatic fever.
Fever with a sandpaper rash, strawberry tongue and circumoral pallor
That describes scarlet fever.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which patient education is given for erythrasma?
opts: Shower after any hot tub use and check the disinfectant level
That belongs to Pseudomonas folliculitis.
Keep the area clean and dry, avoid excessive heat or moisture, and maintain a healthy body weight
Correct — heat and humidity are the favourable conditions for the organism.
Avoid sharing towels, clothing, bath water, washcloths and razors
That is the education for impetigo, which is contagious.
Stop smoking and avoid any constrictive clothing over the affected area at all times
That belongs to hidradenitis suppurativa.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What should be suspected when acne scarring seems out of proportion to the severity of lesions?
opts: An undiagnosed hyperandrogenic state driving deeper inflammation
Hyperandrogenism is suspected from hirsutism and menstrual irregularity.
Resistance of Cutibacterium acnes to the prescribed antimicrobial
Resistance would show as failure to improve, not disproportionate scarring.
An underlying immunodeficiency impairing the healing of each lesion
That is not among the explanations the lecture offers.
Patient manipulation of the lesions through picking or squeezing
Correct. Patients and families are educated about that risk.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which shaving alternatives are named for pseudofolliculitis barbae?
opts: Waxing of the beard area every two weeks under supervision
That is not among the described alternatives.
Weekly application of a topical antibiotic instead of shaving
Topical antibiotics reduce colonisation rather than replace shaving.
Chemical depilatories, which inhibit hair growth, and laser-assisted permanent hair removal
Correct — stopping shaving altogether is the first suggestion.
Electric razors used daily and always against the direction of the hair growth
Cutting the hair below the surface is what causes the problem.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How does the lecture describe the definitive procedure for an abscess that will not drain?
opts: Aspiration with a fine needle under ultrasound guidance
That is not the described procedure.
Observation with warm soaks until it drains on its own
That applies to a lesion that has already drained.
Surgical incision and drainage, covered in detail in a later course
Correct — the aim is to eradicate infection and prevent recurrence.
Wide excision of the affected area under general anaesthesia
That belongs to hidradenitis suppurativa.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which specimens are taken in serious cellulitis?
opts: Perilesional tissue for direct immunofluorescence
That investigates autoimmune blistering disease.
A potassium hydroxide preparation of the leading edge
That would investigate a fungal cause.
Blood cultures and a skin punch biopsy
Correct, alongside a complete blood count and creatine phosphokinase.
A superficial swab of the intact affected skin
A surface swab is not among the described tests.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: A patient with cellulitis remains febrile after fifty hours of oral antibiotics. What should happen?
opts: Continue the same antibiotic, since inflammation takes one to two weeks
Slow resolution of inflammation is expected, but persistent fever is not.
Add a topical antibiotic to the affected area alongside the oral
Topical therapy does not reach deeper dermal infection.
Stop antibiotics entirely and observe for a further forty-eight hours
Stopping treatment in active cellulitis is not appropriate.
Change the antimicrobial therapy, guided by culture results
Correct — fever beyond forty-eight hours is the stated trigger.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How does erysipelas present systemically?
opts: Unrelenting pain out of proportion to examination, with skin colour changing to blue-grey
That describes necrotizing fasciitis.
Sudden onset of malaise, myalgias, chills and high fever within forty-eight hours of skin changes
Correct, with nausea, headache, pruritus, burning, tenderness and swelling.
Gradual onset of low-grade fever and fatigue over the two weeks before the rash appears
The onset is described as sudden, not gradual.
No systemic symptoms at all, with the patient consistently afebrile and otherwise well
That describes folliculitis.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What is the pathophysiology of pseudofolliculitis barbae?
opts: A cut hair curves into the follicular wall and penetrates the skin, causing a foreign body reaction
Correct. It occurs in any shaved area and commonly in Black males with tightly curled facial hair.
Bacteria enter the follicle through a break in the skin and produce a follicular pustule
That is infectious folliculitis rather than this foreign body reaction.
Keratin plugs occlude the pilosebaceous unit and sebum accumulates behind the blockage
That describes the follicular hyperkeratinisation of acne.
Apocrine ducts become obstructed and rupture, seeding inflammation into the dermis
That describes hidradenitis suppurativa.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Where does acne vulgaris rank among skin diseases in the United States?
opts: It is the second most common, affecting about 40% of Americans in their lifetime
The lecture ranks it first, at roughly twice that figure.
It is the most common in adolescents only, affecting about 20% of adults
The 80% figure is a lifetime prevalence across the population.
It is uncommon overall, affecting fewer than 10% of Americans in their lifetime
That substantially understates the stated prevalence.
It is the most common skin disease, affecting about 80% of Americans in their lifetime
Correct. It usually begins with the onset of puberty.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Can antibiotics prevent acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis after impetigo?
opts: Only in children over eight, where doxycycline can be used
Age and agent do not change the lack of prevention.
No, because the immune activation most often precedes antibiotic treatment
Correct — it particularly affects three to seven year olds.
Yes, if started within forty-eight hours of the rash appearing
Prevention is specifically stated not to occur.
Yes, but only where the organism has first been confirmed on culture
Culture status does not change the lack of prevention.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: How does chronic paronychia present, and over what timescale?
opts: Oedematous, erythematous, tender nail folds without fluctuance, present at least six weeks
Correct. Nail plates thicken and discolour, and cuticles separate from the plate.
Rapid onset of erythema and swelling two to five days after trauma, often fluctuant
That describes acute paronychia.
Painless thickening and yellowing of the nail plate over months without inflammation
That describes onychomycosis.
Grouped painful vesicles on the distal finger appearing over twenty-four hours
That describes herpetic whitlow.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which factors predispose to hidradenitis suppurativa?
opts: Hot weather, excessive perspiration, obesity, apocrine duct obstruction, secondary infection and smoking
Correct. Smoking cessation is described as essential in management.
Cold dry weather, low body weight, occupational chemical exposure and repeated hand immersion
Repeated immersion is a predisposing factor for chronic paronychia.
Impaired lymphatic drainage, tinea pedis, obesity and any pre-existing skin infection
Those are the risk factors for erysipelas.
Puberty, androgen excess, genetics, lithium therapy and acnegenic mineral oil exposure
Those are the predisposing factors for acne vulgaris.

set2.io: Objective b — Unique considerations of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus skin infections
set2.q: Which measure is recommended when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is a concern in a drained furuncle?
opts: Culture the material obtained at incision and drainage
Correct, and give endocarditis prophylaxis to at-risk patients.
Start linezolid empirically before any material is obtained
Empiric therapy uses dicloxacillin or cephalexin unless resistance is suspected.
Swab the nasal vestibule of every household contact first
Nasal swabbing is described for recurrent folliculitis.
Defer drainage until the culture result becomes available
Drainage is not delayed for culture.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: When are oral antibiotics indicated in acne vulgaris?
opts: For moderate to severe acne too widespread for topicals, or after an inadequate response over six to eight weeks
Correct, and they are prescribed for the shortest time possible, about three to four months.
For comedonal acne at first presentation, before any topical therapy has been trialled at all
Comedonal acne is treated with a topical retinoid first.
For any patient whose acne has failed to clear completely within two weeks of starting treatment
Improvement in lesions takes four to six weeks.
For patients with acne scarring, in order to prevent any further scars from developing over time
Scarring is not the stated indication for systemic antibiotics.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Why does devitalised tissue in cellulitis require surgical debridement?
opts: It is not perfused, so antibiotics cannot reach the site
Correct — tense, cyanotic, necrotic, bronzed or blanched skin is the clue.
It harbours resistant organisms that no oral antibiotic will cover
The problem is delivery of the drug rather than resistance.
It prevents accurate culture of the organism from the affected area
Culture yield is not the reason debridement is required.
It causes pain that cannot be controlled with systemic analgesia
Pain control is not the stated indication.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What kind of organism is Cutibacterium acnes?
opts: An anaerobic Gram-positive rod that is part of normal skin flora
Correct. It was formerly known as Propionibacterium acnes and promotes inflammation.
An aerobic Gram-negative rod acquired from contaminated water
That describes Pseudomonas aeruginosa in hot tub folliculitis.
An aerobic Gram-positive coccus carried in the nasal vestibule
That describes Staphylococcus aureus.
A dimorphic yeast that colonises moist intertriginous surfaces
That describes Candida albicans in chronic paronychia.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: What proportion of erysipelas cases involve the lower extremities?
opts: About 20%
That understates the figure given.
About 50%
That understates the figure given.
Close to 100%
Facial erysipelas is common enough that this overstates it.
About 80%
Correct — the face is the other common site.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which conditions are named in the differential for folliculitis?
opts: Discoid lupus, deep vein thrombosis and cellulitis
That is the differential for erysipelas.
Necrotizing fasciitis, deep vein thrombosis and contact dermatitis
That is the differential for cellulitis.
Acne, tinea barbae, molluscum contagiosum and eczema
Correct — all four can produce papules in a follicular distribution.
Thermal burn, allergic contact dermatitis and herpes zoster
That is the differential for bullous impetigo.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which single clue is emphasised for recognising necrotizing fasciitis early?
opts: Coral-red fluorescence of the affected skin under a Wood's lamp
That finding points to erythrasma.
Unrelenting pain out of proportion to the physical examination
Correct — patients are often diagnosed with cellulitis, sent home, and return worse.
A sharply demarcated plaque raised above the surrounding skin
That finding points to erysipelas.
Honey-coloured crusting over a superficial epidermal erosion
That finding points to non-bullous impetigo.

set2.io: Objective a — Etiologies, epidemiology, risk factors, manifestations, differential diagnosis, testing, management, referrals, education and prognosis for cutaneous bacterial infections
set2.q: Which tests may be used in acute paronychia and what does each exclude?
opts: Nasal swab for staphylococcal carriage, plucked hair for dermatophytes, biopsy for follicular disease
That workup belongs to resistant folliculitis.
Gram stain and culture for the bacterial cause, potassium hydroxide for candida, Tzanck smear for herpetic whitlow
Correct. It is usually a clinical diagnosis, so testing is directed rather than routine.
Wood's lamp for coral-red fluorescence, potassium hydroxide for dermatophytes, biopsy for malignancy
Wood's lamp examination is the test for erythrasma.
Blood cultures for bacteraemia, creatine phosphokinase for muscle damage, imaging for osteomyelitis
That workup belongs to serious cellulitis.
